name: Read the ledger before you spend
when: a run, an added step or a light call is about to read primary sources about persons or texts the system has read before (the owner, 2026-09-07 18:30: 'later sessions should be able to skim through that and have a map about what is where and thus reduce costs')
shape: before the call: GET /v1/readings?person=<each person the packet names> and ?text=<each uid> — the entries say which job, engine and rows exist and where they render; attach the entries as the packet's `prior_readings` (an added step does this itself); tell the engine to cite prior rows by job and id and to read only what is new; skip a text whose windows were read for the same question unless the question changed
ingredients: the persons and texts the packet names
the readings ledger (index by person, surname, text, job)
the renders (/oeuvre, /distinctions, /encounter, /reread) for a reader who wants the rows in words
yields: fewer re-readings of the same texts for the same questions; a run that starts from what is known (the Hintze encounter can start from the distinction round's I2 rows on Hintze rather than re-reading the essay)
misses: rows made before the ledger existed unless a session backfills them (POST /v1/readings/index/{job_id}); a person named differently across runs (the surname index catches most)
origin: the owner's rule after the Hintze encounter, 2026-09-07; the ledger is written by code when a phase or an added step finishes
note: The Stacks attach the same readings to the author's and the text's records; the Referee to the thinker.
